input.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION
input.rationale: The cap is mutual and nominally 12-month based, but it is narrowed to amounts paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to", i.e. materially less than 12 months' fees, and the only carve-out is Section 8 (indemnification). Confidentiality (Section 10), gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud sit inside the cap, so the clause fails the fallback which requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Redline restores a full 12-month fee cap and adds an Excluded Claims sentence; the mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages is acceptable as drafted.

input.quote: Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
input.rationale: Commerce One gives a full IP infringement indemnity covering us and our Customers, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and procure-modify-replace-or-refund remedies, and only the usual exclusions (use outside Documentation, third-party modification). The indemnity sits entirely outside the Section 9 cap, which is better than the fallback super-cap, and there is no reciprocal Customer indemnity. Preferred extras (breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) are absent but that is short of the preferred wording only, not a fallback failure.
